sum: Flex Ltd. provides technology innovation, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions to data center, communications, enterprise, consumer, automotive, healthcare, industrial, and power industries in the Americas, Asia, and Europe. The company operates through three segments: Integrated Technology Solutions (ITS), Regulated Manufacturing Solutions (RMS), and Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI). The ITS segment offers flexible supply and manufacturing solutions for communications, including high speed networking, enterprise, and satellite communications systems, as well as lifestyle solutions comprising products across commercial, home, and personal product categories. Its RMS segment includes industrial products, such as mission critical automation, energy, and industrial infrastructure; automotive products, including compute and power electronics platforms and integrated systems; and healthcare products comprising regulated manufacturing for medical devices, drug delivery, and equipment. The CPI segment provides cloud and cooling products, such as integrated compute systems supporting power dense digital infrastructure deployments and advanced liquid cooling solutions supporting higher density, power intensive rack architectures; and power products that include utility and facility level electrical infrastructure enabling power delivery and high density rack and board level power systems. The company was formerly known as Flextronics International Ltd. and changed its name to Flex Ltd. in September 2016. Flex Ltd. was founded in 1969 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

On November 2, 2026, Flex Ltd. (“Flex” or the “Company”) held an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (the “Extraordinary General Meeting”) in connection with the proposed separation of Flex’s cloud and power infrastructure business. There were 369,460,443 Ordinary Shares of Flex, no par value (“Ordinary Shares”), issued and outstanding and entitled to be voted at the Extraordinary General Meeting. At the Extraordinary General Meeting, a total of 312,465,705 Ordinary Shares were represented in person or by proxy, or approximately 84.57% of the issued and outstanding Ordinary Shares, and, therefore, a quorum was present. 
 At the Extraordinary General Meeting, Flex shareholders approved all three proposals, which are summarized below and described in detail in the Company’s definitive proxy statement, dated October 5, 2026, and first mailed to the Company’s shareholders on or about the date thereof. The Company’s Inspector of Elections certified the following vote tabulations on the proposals from the Extraordinary General Meeting: 
 Meeting Proposal 1 – Ordinary Resolution: 
 To approve the proposed issuance of one (1) Bonus Share for every one (1) existing Flex ordinary share held by each Flex shareholder of record as of the date to be set by the Flex Board of Directors or an officer authorized to make such determination by the Board of Directors to determine the Flex shareholders eligible to receive the Bonus Shares and the distribution of Axiom Solutions International, Inc. common stock (“Record Date”).
